title: A flag flutters in a 6 m/s wind

fluid.source: Incropera, DeWitt, Bergman and Lavine, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, 6th ed. (2007), table A.4 (air at 300 K and 1 atm): nu 15.89e-6 m2/s, rho 1.1614 kg/m3, 300 K; typed from the table, not re-checked against a copy in this session

material.source: flag cloth of about 60 g/m2 at 0.1 mm, as ripstop nylon; stretch stiffness E h = 600 N/m, the soft small-strain range of a woven cloth (crimp), which keeps it within 0.2 % of its length under this wind; bending as a plate of that modulus (demonstration values, not measured on a cloth; taken as isotropic). A stiffer cloth needs a finer flow step: the flow must follow its stretch waves (docs/lab/fsi.md)
